The plan never states the per-edge orthogonal residuals or their dimensions (the table); S5.4.4 only asserts comparable nondegenerate labels and the single decreasing edge, with data and sink edges 'zero or nonnegative'.
S5.4.3 gives only the inclusion <t_X> in t_Y^perp from t_X perp t_Y; the complement <t_X,t_Y>^perp of dimension h-2 for edge 2 to 5 is not stated.

The plan only presupposes an orthonormal basis of each residual (S5.5, S5.5.1); it never states that nonzero residuals over F_2 are nondegenerate and nonalternating nor how alternating planes are absorbed.
S5.4.6 states L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539, both below 1/2.
S5.5.1 gives wt(z+w)=wt(z)+wt(w)-2|supp∩supp|, additivity mod 4 when z.w=0, and q_V-q_U=sum wt(v)[v.x] over an orthonormal basis of the residual.
S5.5.2 gives norm one hence odd weight, phase i^{eps[v.x]}=(1+i^eps)/2+(1-i^eps)/2 (-1)^{v.x}, and after conjugating by H it is the translation kernel aI+bX_v or its inverse.

The plan states one kernel per residual basis vector and the count s_c (S5.5, S5.5.3) but never the tensoring over k columns, i.e. that each residual vector gives one factor acting on all k columns; no step mentions columns in this sense.

S5.7 only states the factorization A=E1 Pi E2 with Pi having a ones (quote is the lemma statement); the elimination proof (pivot at rightmost entry of topmost nonzero row, lower-triangular clearing, repeat on active indices) is not given.

The plan states E=64(W+m+1)^3, B=s+E, nu=min{j>=1: m^j>=B}, C_1=max{20,nu+3}, C_0=128mB^2 and Delta=ceil(C_0 d^{C_1}); the nu=11 value is not given but S8.1.1 has C_1=20.

summary: 19 of 26 present, 7 absent, 0 wrong. The plan carries all of B1-B4, the L3 and L5 numerics, P1-P2, the R-chain, M3-M4 and all of S1-S5. It omits the residual table (L1), the h-2 complement on the side edge (L2), the nonalternating/orthonormal-basis argument (L4), the k-column tensoring (P3), the endpoint frames and Z-repair details of the exceptional pair (P4), the elimination proof (M1) and the choice of the prime avoiding denominators (M2).
